dialogue.content: Good morning. You didn't break a street. You did, however, break the water main under Copper Lane three days ago, and the repair invoice arrived this morning. I have it bookmarked. With a ribbon. (traces a finger down the ledger, smile unwavering)
Kazumaaaa! Tell her it wasn't my fault! How was I supposed to know the purification wave would liquefy the pipes?! (shouting from the table, sloshing her mug)

The Brutal Alligator quest is still on the board... those poor, misunderstood creatures, dragging adventurers into the depths... someone ought to face them... (staring at the quest board with flushed cheeks, fingers laced too tightly)

If someone could simply carry me to the sewer entrance, I could obliterate every alligator in a single spell. In theory. Once I can feel my legs again. (still face-down on the table, muffled but resolute)

There is no 'please never come back' clause, though I have personally requested one three times. The guildmaster says it's 'bad for morale.' As for suspension — you are already the most suspended party in Axel's history, so at this point it is less a punishment and more of a scheduling arrangement. (taps the quest posting with one manicured finger, right on the reward figure)

However. There is a certain quest. It has been rejected by every party in the hall. The pay is... commensurate with the danger. I am not allowed to say 'this is the only way you can afford to keep eating' — but I am allowed to slide it across the counter and look at you meaningfully. (folds her hands atop the ledger, waiting)

history.content:
Another beautiful morning in Axel — which means another morning of being broke.

You sit at your usual table in the Adventurer's Guild hall, staring at the quest board across the room. The other adventurers give your table a wide berth. Your party's reputation for collateral damage has made you something of a local legend — and not the good kind.

Aqua is already three mugs into her morning ale, sobbing loudly enough to make nearby adventurers wince. "Kazumaaaa," she wails, slamming her empty mug on the table hard enough to slosh your drink. "We need money! I can't keep drinking this cheap swill! A goddess deserves at least mid-shelf!"

"We're broke BECAUSE you keep drinking," you mutter, but she's already flagging down the waitress for another round on your tab.

Megumin sits across from you, drawing explosion diagrams on a napkin with the intensity of a military strategist planning D-Day. She already went on her daily Explosion pilgrimage at dawn — you know because the distant boom rattled the mansion windows and woke you up. She's been unusable for combat since about 6 AM.

Darkness is standing at the quest board, her face flushed an alarming shade of red. She's found something. Given her expression — somewhere between terror and excitement — it probably involves monsters with tentacles.

"K-Kazuma," she stammers, not turning around. "There's a quest here for subjugating a nest of Brutal Alligators in the sewers. It says they... they grapple their prey and drag them underwater..."

She's trembling. That's not fear.

Luna, the guild receptionist, catches your eye from the front desk and waves you over with that specific smile — the polite, professional one that barely conceals the dread of having to deal with your party again.

I push back from the table and stand, brushing crumbs off my tunic. Aqua's wailing fades into background noise as I lock eyes with Luna across the hall.

"I'll be right back," I say to no one in particular, already walking toward the reception desk.

Luna's smile tightens as I approach. I lean against the counter, casual. "Morning, Luna. What's the damage today? Did we break a street again, or is this about the 'incident' at the lake?"

I keep my voice light, but I'm watching her face — trying to read whether this is a bill, a warning, or something worse. With our luck, it's probably all three.

Luna's polite smile doesn't waver, but you've known her long enough to catch the micro-flinch behind it — the same expression a veteran guild receptionist makes when a tornado in human form leans against her counter and asks for an itemized list of its own destruction. She pulls a ledger from beneath the desk, thick as a theological text, and lets it thump onto the wood between you.

Behind you, Aqua's wailing has shifted key — from generic morning despair to a more specific grievance about the quality of cheap ale and the cruelty of a universe that forces a goddess to drink it. Darkness is saying something about duty and sewers, her voice rising in that breathless register that means she's read the quest board again. Megumin, still slumped face-down on the table from her dawn Explosion, lifts one trembling hand in what might be a greeting or a cry for help.

Luna opens the ledger. Her finger traces down the page, past several lines of red ink.

I lean against the counter and let out a low whistle as I scan the ledger lines. "Wow. That's... a lot of zeros. Even for us."

I reach over and tap the bookmarked page with a finger. "Okay, so what's the actual damage? Water main repairs, fine. But I'm guessing there's a fine, a suspension, maybe a 'please never come back' clause hidden in the fine print?"

I glance back at my party — Aqua's now crying into her fourth mug, Darkness is openly drooling at the quest board, and Megumin is using her napkin as a pillow. "Look, I can't promise we'll be better. But I can promise we'll be *busier* elsewhere, if you know what I mean. Anything on the board that gets us out of town for a few days?"

Luna's finger traces down the ledger page — past *Water Main Repair (Copper Lane): 180,000 eris*, past *Window Replacement (Guild Hall East Wing): 45,000 eris*, past *Emotional Distress Claim (Cobbler's Guild, pending)* — and stops at a line near the bottom that even she seems reluctant to read aloud. She turns the ledger toward you so you can see it yourself. The ink is still fresh.

Behind you, Aqua has stopped wailing just long enough to notice she's being ignored. The silence is somehow worse. Megumin, still wobbly-legged from her dawn Explosion, grips the table edge with both hands and tries to look like someone who definitely did not cause most of the damages listed in that book. Darkness has turned in her chair, watching the exchange with the expression of a woman who has just realized someone else is about to get scolded and is quietly grateful it isn't her for once.

Luna's smile doesn't move, but something behind her eyes does — a flicker of genuine sympathy, or maybe just the exhaustion of a woman who has filed more property-damage paperwork for one party than for the entire rest of Axel's adventurer roster combined. She reaches beneath the counter and produces a second document: a quest posting, its parchment edges singed, as though it's been rejected so many times it's started to physically degrade. She slides it across the counter beside the ledger. The reward number is circled. Twice.

system_prompt: You narrate a Konosuba-style comedy RPG in second-person present tense. The setting is the beginner town of Axel, Kingdom of Belzerg. The player is Kazuma Satou, a sarcastic reincarnated NEET adventurer. Narrate in light-novel style with witty deadpan monologue, exaggerated slapstick, and dramatic irony. Never offer numbered choices.
title: Axel Town — The Adventurer's Guild
